subject: Geography
central_question: What evidence and mechanisms explain the changing positions of continents and oceans through continental drift, sea-floor spreading and plate tectonics?
in_scope_units: Continental drift, Pangaea, Panthalassa, Laurasia and Gondwanaland.
Evidence from continental fit, rocks, tillite, placer deposits and fossils.
Wegener’s proposed forces and post-drift convection ideas.
Ocean-floor configuration and earthquake and volcano patterns.
Plate tectonics, plate boundaries and movement of the Indian Plate.
banned_topics: Detailed seismic-wave structure, which belongs to Interior of the Earth.
Detailed erosion and weathering, which belong to Geomorphic Processes.
Detailed Indian physiography, which belongs to Structure and Physiography.

known_pitfalls.claim: Continents have always occupied present positions.
known_pitfalls.correction: Wegener argued that they were once united in Pangaea.

known_pitfalls.claim: The modern shoreline gives the best fit.
Wegener’s forces were accepted as adequate.
known_pitfalls.correction: Most scholars considered them too weak.
Hess proposed creation at ridges and consumption at trenches.

known_pitfalls.claim: Continents move independently over ocean floor.
known_pitfalls.correction: Continents are parts of moving lithospheric plates.

recommended_example_progression: Use Exercise 2(i) to explain Wegener’s forces.
Use Exercise 2(iii) to compare boundary types.
Use Exercise 3(i) to organise drift evidence.
Use Exercise 3(ii–iii) to compare theories and post-drift discoveries.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Exercises 1(i–v), 2(i–iv), 3(i–iii), and a Project Work task on earthquake damage.
